picks.intervention_label: Daraxonrasib / elironrasib / zoldonrasib (RAS(ON)) + ivonescimab ± cetuximab (NCT07397338)
picks.rationale: This is the one trial where the A59T allele reads eligible on its face — the gate asks only for a documented KRAS/HRAS/NRAS mutation, no codon restriction, unlike the codon-12/13/61 RMC-6236 basket that shut the patient out. The upside is the whole ballgame: RAS(ON) glues bind GTP-loaded RAS at a site A59T does not disrupt, and the tool-compound package showed regression across G12/G13/Q61 PDAC/CRC/NSCLC models (pmid:38778099, pmid:38778097), so a switch-II mutant is a plausible extension rather than a stretch. I will say plainly that no published A59T regression curve exists — this rides on mechanism plus a US-accessible Revolution sponsor, and the added ivonescimab/cetuximab arm keeps the anti-EGFR question live in a RAS-mutant patient.
primary_concerns: Zero direct A59T efficacy data — the entire case is a read-across from G12/G13/Q61 preclinical work, so the effect could be far smaller than the headline models suggest
Sponsor may still interpret 'documented RAS mutation' as canonical codons at screening; the eligibility win needs a local-PI confirmation call before it is real
RAS(ON) plus a PD-1/VEGF bispecific is a heavy combination with overlapping GI/rash/hepatic toxicity, and this patient has a peri-HIPEC surgical window to protect

picks.intervention_label: Botensilimab + balstilimab (Fc-enhanced anti-CTLA-4 + anti-PD-1) (NCT05608044)
picks.rationale: The patient is the exact phenotype where bot/bal actually worked — peritoneal-dominant disease after liver-met resection is the no-liver-mets subset that hit ORR 22% and mOS 20.9 mo where the liver-mets group managed only 5% (pmid:38871975). The randomized update called out confirmed responses at peritoneal sites specifically, which is this patient's whole disease compartment. MSS/TMB-low usually kills the immuno-oncology conversation, but Fc-enhanced CTLA-4 is the one construct with a real MSS signal, and I would rather chase a 20%-plus response at the right anatomy than write immunotherapy off on marker status alone.
primary_concerns: Eligibility is 2L+ — the patient is on 1L FOLFIRI-bev now and has to progress before enrolling, which the pick's timing depends on
G3+ immune-mediated AE rate around 35% (colitis, hepatitis) is not trivial ahead of major cytoreductive surgery
The A59T immuno-oncology-enrichment literature does not apply here: this patient is MSS/TMB-low/PD-L1-neg, the opposite of the A59T-enriched pattern (pmid:33945173), so response is not a given

picks.intervention_label: CGT6297 mutant-selective PI3K-alpha inhibitor, CRC + PIK3CA cohort (NCT07383506)
picks.rationale: This is the cleanest PIK3CA-and-CRC match on the board — phase 1b Cohort 3 names PIK3CA-mutant colorectal cancer explicitly, and M1043I is a kinase-domain activating allele that fits the oncogenic-mutation gate. The upside case is a mutant-selective agent that hits the driver while sparing wild-type PI3K, which is what limited alpelisib (G3+ hyperglycemia ~20%, pmid:29401002); the double-mutant biology (pmid:31699932) and INAVO120's HR 0.43 in PIK3CA-mutant breast (pmid:39476340) say this axis is genuinely druggable. I concede the CRC PI3K-alpha monotherapy track record is thin — 2 CRC PRs of 134 in the alpelisib first-in-human — so the real play may be pairing this with the RAS-pathway pick rather than solo.
primary_concerns: KRAS co-activation historically blunts PI3K-alpha monotherapy in CRC — vertical RAS+PI3K blockade is the mechanistically sound play but doubles the toxicity load
M1043I is a non-canonical hotspot (not H1047R/E545K), so 'oncogenic PIK3CA' eligibility and mutant-selectivity against this specific allele both need confirming
Diabetes and prior PI3K/AKT/mTOR exposure gate enrollment; hyperglycemia management overlaps poorly with the peri-operative window

picks.intervention_label: PF-07934040 pan-KRAS inhibitor ± cetuximab / FOLFOX / bevacizumab (NCT06447662)
picks.rationale: For CRC the inclusion text reads 'confirmed KRAS mutation, any variant' — the most unambiguous codon-agnostic gate among the small-molecule KRAS programs, and it covers A59T without a sponsor-interpretation asterisk. The upside is a direct-to-KRAS small molecule (not a downstream MEK/ERK detour) with a US Pfizer sponsor and cetuximab/bev combination arms that fit a bevacizumab-experienced patient. Same honest caveat as every entry in this class: no A59T-specific data exists, so this is a mechanism bet backed by the cleanest eligibility language on the list.
primary_concerns: Phase 1 dose-escalation — RP2D and any A59T activity are both unknown, and early cohorts may be sub-therapeutic
'Any variant' pan-KRAS binders are still overwhelmingly optimized against G12/G13; switch-II A59 engagement is assumed, not shown
2-3L CRC cohort requires prior fluoropyrimidine plus oxaliplatin and/or irinotecan, so timing sits past current 1L

picks.intervention_label: NST-628 pan-RAF/MEK molecular glue (NCT06326411)
picks.rationale: If the RAS(ON) and pan-KRAS gates stall at sponsor review, NST-628 is the downstream fallback — it acts at RAF/MEK below the specific RAS allele, so an A59T that activates the MAPK cascade is engaged regardless of the mutation site, and Part B lists KRAS activating mutations without codon limits. The upside is a MAPK-node bet that does not care whether A59T is 'canonical.' I rank it fifth, not higher, because MEK-node drugs have a long history of clinical underperformance in MSS CRC (IMblaze370, pmid:30975633-adjacent) and single-node MAPK inhibition rarely holds RAS-driven tumors for long.
primary_concerns: RAF/MEK-node inhibitors have repeatedly disappointed in RAS-mutant CRC; feedback reactivation of the pathway is the expected failure mode
Prior MEK or BRAF inhibitor exposure excludes — fine now, but it burns a bridge for later MAPK options
Molecular-glue class is early; RP2D, durability, and A59T activity are all unestablished

picks.intervention_label: DT2216 BCL-xL PROTAC degrader (± irinotecan) (NCT06964009 / NCT06620302)
picks.rationale: The 20q11 amplification is real and gene-level actionable: BCL2L1-amplified CRC lines were 10-100x more sensitive to BCL-xL inhibition than non-amplified lines (pmid:26715361), and the PROTAC solves the navitoclax thrombocytopenia problem by sparing platelets (pmid:31792461). With TOP1 co-amplified on the same segment, the DT2216-plus-irinotecan pairing lines up with the patient's existing irinotecan backbone — a genuine two-hit rationale rather than a single marker. The sober read: the first-in-human DT2216 monotherapy gave stable disease only (no objective responses, n=20), so this earns its keep as a rational combination partner, not a standalone.
primary_concerns: Monotherapy signal is SD-only so far; the whole thesis rests on chemo/RAS-inhibitor combination synergy that has not been tested in a BCL2L1-amplified CRC patient
Access is the real barrier — the recruiting DT2216 combination trials are ovarian (paclitaxel) and pediatric (irinotecan), so this needs a compassionate-use or off-label path
On-target thrombocytopenia, even if platelet-sparing versus navitoclax, complicates a peri-operative bleeding window

notes: Efficacy-weighted case (0.70), prefers_trials true, no toxicity vetoes — my picks lean hard into the codon-agnostic RAS programs the re-run surfaced. The honest through-line: every pan-RAS/pan-KRAS pick here rides mechanism, not A59T efficacy data, because none exists (the Arena/Siena functional work, pmid:34031055, is the closest thing and it only says A59 signals variably). I deliberately weighted eligibility language: NCT07397338, NCT06447662, and NCT07383506 have the cleanest codon-agnostic or CRC-PIK3CA gates and US sponsors, which is why the China-based pan-RAS trials (YL-17231, GH55, BPI-572270) and the Russia MEK+HCQ trial did not make my ranked list despite matching biomarkers. Sequencing note for the board: ranks 1/4/5 need 2L+ progression or sponsor confirmation, so they are not day-one moves — the immediate actionable is banking the comprehensive NGS (VAF, HER2, TP53 substitution) that gates half of these. I did not pick anti-EGFR (Lochhead single PR, pmid:28404754, sits against the Sorich meta-analysis HR 1.08, pmid:25115304) — even for a risktaker, a tier-5 n=1 against a tier-1a null is not upside, it is noise.

picks.intervention_label: Continue FOLFIRI + bevacizumab (current 1L), with DPYD/UGT1A1 genotyping ordered before the next cycle and the regimen paused around the cytoreductive-surgery-plus-HIPEC window
picks.rationale: The regimen the patient is already on carries the deepest OS follow-up of anything on this board. The FOLFIRI-bev backbone rests on AVF2107g (Hurwitz 2004, mOS 20.3 vs 15.6 mo, HR 0.66) and BICC-C (Fuchs 2007), replicated across two decades of registry use, and the toxicity is the one every GI oncologist already manages: cytopenias, diarrhea, mucositis, the bevacizumab hypertension/proteinuria/wound-healing set. That last point is the load-bearing one here, because bevacizumab has to be held roughly 4-6 weeks around the CRS-HIPEC procedure for wound healing, and that pause is a solved logistics problem, not a research question. What is missing today is two cheap safety data points: DPYD (four CPIC variants) and UGT1A1 *6/*28. The 2026 NCCN colon guideline now recommends discussing DPYD before fluoropyrimidine, and cumulative-toxicity carriers can compensate through the first cycles and then decompensate; ordering both before the next cycle costs a blood tube and closes a known 5-FU / irinotecan toxicity gap ahead of the peri-operative window. I am not ranking this first because it targets the KRAS A59T or PIK3CA M1043I biology. I am ranking it first because it is the safest way to hold disease while the confirmatory NGS resolves the five pending gates the fancier options depend on.
primary_concerns: Bevacizumab must be held about 4-6 weeks before and after CRS-HIPEC for wound healing and anastomotic integrity; build that pause into the sequencing plan explicitly rather than discovering it at the pre-op visit.

DPYD and UGT1A1 are not yet resolved. The patient has tolerated cycles so far, but heterozygous DPYD carriers (c.2846A>T, HapB3) show cumulative rather than first-cycle toxicity; document both genotypes before the next fluoropyrimidine/irinotecan exposure.
This is disease-holding, not feature-targeting. Do not let a comfortable 1L backbone delay the confirmatory FoundationOne-class NGS that gates every downstream A59T and PIK3CA decision.

picks.intervention_label: Low-dose aspirin 160 mg PO daily as a PIK3CA-directed adjunct layered onto the systemic backbone, timed around bleeding-risk and surgical windows
picks.rationale: This is the pick that best fits a do-no-harm prior: a biomarker-matched signal, a phase-3 randomized readout, and a drug whose safety profile has decades of post-marketing characterization and an established bleeding-management algorithm. ALASCCA (Frodin 2025, NEJM, n=626, RoB2:Low) randomized resected CRC with a PI3K-pathway alteration to aspirin 160 mg/d for 3 years and hit its primary endpoint: Group A (PIK3CA exon 9/20) time-to-recurrence HR 0.49 (0.24-0.98), 3-yr recurrence 7.7% vs 14.1%. The patient's M1043I is a kinase-domain (exon 20) allele, so it maps into Group A. The AE picture is the reason I can rank this so high without hedging on tolerability: G3+ bleeding was about 3% aspirin vs 2% placebo, serious AEs about 5%, no discontinuation-driving excess. Two honest caveats keep this at rank 2 rather than higher: ALASCCA studied the resected adjuvant setting, not metastatic peritoneal disease, so the effect size does not transfer verbatim; and aspirin on top of bevacizumab plus an imminent major cytoreductive operation raises a real bleeding-timing question. That is a manageable question, not a veto - hold aspirin peri-operatively per surgical protocol and re-time it into the adjuvant-equivalent post-HIPEC window where the ALASCCA evidence actually lives.
primary_concerns: ALASCCA is an adjuvant-setting trial; the patient is metastatic with peritoneal disease. Mechanism and class safety transfer cleanly, the effect size does not - frame this as a low-risk adjunct, not a disease-controlling agent.

Bleeding timing is the one real safety interaction: aspirin plus bevacizumab plus a planned CRS-HIPEC. Hold aspirin peri-operatively per surgical protocol and reintroduce in the post-HIPEC maintenance window.
Confirm M1043I is somatic and clonal on the pending NGS before leaning on the Group A read-across; a subclonal PIK3CA call weakens the biomarker match.

picks.intervention_label: mFOLFOX6 + bevacizumab as the reserved backbone-switch option (or FOLFIRI-aflibercept / FOLFIRI-ramucirumab if oxaliplatin is sequenced first), held for post-HIPEC or on FOLFIRI-bev progression
picks.rationale: The purpose of ranking a second cytotoxic backbone is to have a proven, AE-characterized next step already staged rather than reaching for a phase-1 novelty at first progression. Oxaliplatin-plus-bevacizumab has category-1-level support (NO16966, Saltz 2008, mPFS 9.4 vs 8.0 mo, HR 0.83), and if the sequence instead runs FOLFOX first then FOLFIRI second, the 2L anti-angiogenic swap-ins are equally well characterized: aflibercept (VELOUR, mOS 13.5 vs 12.1 mo, HR 0.82) and ramucirumab (RAISE, mOS 13.3 vs 11.7 mo, HR 0.84). The toxicity that has to be watched and is fully mapped is oxaliplatin cumulative sensory neuropathy, which argues for a stop-and-go or OPTIMOX-style schedule to protect a 30-something patient's long-term function. This also intersects the HIPEC agent choice: if the surgical team uses oxaliplatin HIPEC, systemic oxaliplatin exposure has to be accounted against cumulative neuropathy. All of this is standard sequencing hygiene with published management, which is exactly why it outranks the investigational options below.
primary_concerns: Oxaliplatin cumulative sensory neuropathy is the dominant long-term toxicity in a young patient; plan a stop-and-go schedule and track cumulative dose, especially if oxaliplatin HIPEC is also used.
PRODIGE 7 showed oxaliplatin HIPEC did not add OS over CRS alone; do not let a backbone-switch decision quietly justify an oxaliplatin-HIPEC choice that the randomized data does not support.
This is a reserved option, not an immediate action - promote it only on documented FOLFIRI-bev progression or as post-HIPEC maintenance sequencing.

picks.intervention_label: Inavolisib 9 mg PO QD + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV Q3W on INTRINSIC (NCT04929223), reserved for 2L after documented FOLFIRI-bev progression, with mutant-selective PI3K-alpha trials (RLY-2608 ReDiscover, tersolisib NCT05768139, CGT6297 NCT07383506) flagged as better-tolerated alternatives if a CRC slot is open
picks.rationale: Among the PI3K-alpha-selective options this is the one with the cleanest characterized safety and a defensible biomarker route, which is why it sits ahead of the pan-RAS agents. The registrational anchor is cross-tumor: INAVO120 (Jhaveri 2024, NEJM, n=325, RoB2:Low) at PFS HR 0.43 (0.32-0.59), mPFS 15.0 vs 7.3 mo in HR+/HER2- breast, with a characterized and manageable AE set - G3+ hyperglycemia 5.6% (any-grade 58.6%), G3+ stomatitis 5.6%, G3+ diarrhea 3.7%, discontinuation 6.5%. That runs cleaner than alpelisib (G3+ hyperglycemia about 20%, Juric 2018). The binding weakness is CRC activity: the mCRC translation lives in 2 PRs across the CRC subset of Juric's n=134 plus an INTRINSIC arm that has not posted full data, and M1043I is non-canonical relative to H1047R/E545K/E542K. I want to name the newer data honestly rather than ignore it: the mutant-selective allosteric PI3K-alpha agents now show a materially better tolerability profile in the kinase-domain subgroup - RLY-2608 + fulvestrant gave kinase-domain-PIK3CA ORR 66.7% (38.4-88.2) with G3+ hyperglycemia only ~3% (Sammons 2025), and tersolisib/STX-478 reported no G3+ hyperglycemia, rash, mucositis, or diarrhea at the 100 mg MTD (Montero 2024). Those are breast/gyn populations on abstract-tier data, so I will not promote them over an INTRINSIC route that at least enrolls CRC on a companion diagnostic - but if a CRC cohort opens (CGT6297 explicitly lists a CRC-PIK3CA cohort), the wild-type-sparing safety profile makes them the more do-no-harm PI3K-alpha play. Any of these is a 2L-reserve decision: prove progression, confirm M1043I somatic/clonal, and get fasting glucose and HbA1c with a hyperglycemia algorithm in place first.
primary_concerns: CRC activity is the binding evidence gap. INAVO120 read out in breast; do not let the HR 0.43 breast anchor drive an off-label CRC decision before the INTRINSIC arm-specific data posts. The newer mutant-selective agents are cleaner on tolerability but sit on breast/gyn abstract-tier data with no CRC efficacy readout.

Hyperglycemia management must be pre-loaded: fasting glucose and HbA1c at baseline, endocrine input if HbA1c >=7%, metformin pathway ready. Any-grade hyperglycemia was 58.6% in INAVO120 - characterized, but not trivial in a peri-operative patient.
M1043I is non-canonical; confirm somatic status, kinase-domain activation, and clonal VAF before committing. Predictive confidence for a rarer kinase-domain allele is lower than for H1047R.

picks.intervention_label: Botensilimab + balstilimab (Agenus C-1101 / CCTG NCT07152821; USC any-KRAS MSS trial NCT06336902), reserved for 2L+ after FOLFIRI-bev progression, with a documented immune-toxicity management pathway
picks.rationale: This is the one immunotherapy option with a real MSS-CRC signal at the patient's exact disease site, and I am ranking it deliberately behind the chemo backbone and the PIK3CA adjuncts because the toxicity is the part that has to be respected. The signal is genuine: Bullock 2024 (Nat Med, n=101) gave ORR 22% in the no-liver-metastasis subset - which is this patient's phenotype after liver-met resection - and the randomized phase-2 update specifically called out confirmed responses at peritoneal sites, the dominant compartment here, with mOS approaching two years in NLM patients. That is the strongest MSS-CRC ICI readout of the modern era and it is not a single-agent-ICI-in-MSS mistake. What keeps it at rank 5 is the Fc-enhanced CTLA-4 toxicity: G3+ treatment-related AEs about 35-38%, G3+ immune-mediated diarrhea/colitis 12-13%, G3+ hepatitis about 8%, plus the characteristic pyrexia/cytokine-release picture. There were no treatment-related deaths across the reported cohorts, and the irAE set has an established steroid/infliximab management algorithm - but this needs a center comfortable running that algorithm, and it needs to sit after the patient has progressed on the standard backbone. It is a 2L+ reserve with eyes open, not a first move.
primary_concerns: G3+ immune-mediated toxicity is the gating issue: diarrhea/colitis 12-13%, hepatitis ~8%, overall G3+ TRAE ~35-38%. Enroll only at a site with a standing irAE algorithm (steroid taper, infliximab for steroid-refractory colitis) and baseline hepatic/endocrine monitoring.

The peritoneal-site response signal is from an abstract-tier randomized phase-2 update; the CCTG phase 3 (NCT07152821) is the confirmatory step and is not yet mature. Treat the ORR as promising, not established.
Sequencing: the biomarker-eligible trials require prior fluoropyrimidine/oxaliplatin/irinotecan progression, so this is genuinely a 2L+ option - do not pull it forward ahead of the proven backbone.

notes: Posture: hold the standard-of-care floor and rank every novel-mechanism option strictly behind proven 1L/2L sequencing and behind the one biomarker-matched adjunct that carries phase-3 evidence plus decades of safety data (aspirin, ALASCCA 2025). The re-run's headline change from my prior position is that I moved aspirin up to rank 2 - the ALASCCA readout is exactly the profile a do-no-harm prior rewards: RoB2:Low phase 3, biomarker-matched to M1043I (Group A, exon 20), G3+ bleeding ~3% with a fully-mapped management algorithm. On the pan-RAS agents I was asked to weigh honestly: I am deliberately NOT ranking daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) or the even-earlier codon-agnostic programs (NST-628 NCT06326411, darlifarnib/KO-2806 NCT06026410, PF-07934040 NCT06447662, RO7673396 NCT06884618, ERAS-0015 NCT06983743, AN9025, YL-17231, GH55, BPI-572270) into my top 5. The mechanistic rationale for reaching switch-II A59T is real and structurally coherent (Knox 2025 J Med Chem: binds outside the mutated codon groove), but the safety and efficacy picture does not clear my bar: the pivotal daraxonrasib dataset (Wolpin 2026 NEJM) is PDAC on codon-12/13/61 alleles with G3+ treatment-related AEs in 30% (rash, stomatitis, diarrhea), the CRC monotherapy ORR was only 9% (RevMed corporate update, unpublished, no CIs), and there is zero A59T-specific efficacy or long-tail toxicity data anywhere. Named missing datum: no A59T-specific response or dedicated combination-toxicity readout for any pan-RAS agent. That is a maturity/tolerability deprioritization, not a novelty penalty - if the RevMed sponsor confirms A59T eligibility on NCT06445062 or NCT07397338 it becomes a legitimate trial referral, but it belongs below the characterized options, not among them. Two contested items I expect to critique downstream: (1) any rank-1 pan-RAS pick from the risktaker on effect-size-over-evidence grounds, and if a daraxonrasib-plus-chemo or daraxonrasib-plus-cetuximab arm is proposed I will dissent on toxicity given the 30% G3+ TRAE has no characterized combination-toxicity dataset in CRC; (2) an advocate or concensusite HER2 pick (T-DXd, tucatinib) - HER2 is not reported yet and MOUNTAINEER's RAS-WT gate is failed by A59T, so I will qualify on guideline_fit until the pending NGS returns ERBB2. No toxicity_vetoes are declared in preferences.json, so I hold no standing round-2 veto trigger; any veto I issue will be reasoned from combination-toxicity incompatibility, not from a stated user veto. Standard caveat carried forward: oxaliplatin HIPEC did not add OS over CRS alone in PRODIGE 7, so the HIPEC-agent choice should not be treated as a survival-driving decision.

picks.intervention_label: Low-dose aspirin 160 mg PO QD as post-CRS adjuvant-equivalent maintenance in the PIK3CA-pathway-altered patient, sequenced around the surgical bleeding window
picks.rationale: This is the only RoB2:Low randomized phase 3 in the dossier where the biomarker matches the patient and the pre-specified primary endpoint actually cleared alpha. ALASCCA (Frödin 2025 NEJM, n=626, aspirin 160 mg vs placebo x3 yr) hit HR 0.49 for time to recurrence in Group A (PIK3CA exon 9/20, which is the allele class M1043I sits in), 95% CI 0.24-0.98, p=0.044; Group B ran HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.21-0.83. The direction replicates in the pre-specified PIK3CA-activating subgroup of CALGB/SWOG 80702 (celecoxib DFS HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.35-0.88; OS HR 0.41, 95% CI 0.21-0.79) and in the Liao 2012 NHS+HPFS observational data (HR 0.18, 95% CI 0.06-0.61). Three datasets, two of them RCT-grade, all pointing the same way, with a coherent COX-2 / PGE2 / PI3K mechanism underneath. What I won't paper over: every one of those trials enrolled resected stage I-III disease, not stage IV with active peritoneal spread. The biology travels to this patient; the trial population does not. So I rank it first as a feature-targeting adjunct for the post-CRS window, not as antitumor therapy for active metastatic disease, and the whole thing rides on top of a real chemo backbone, not instead of one.
primary_concerns: Indication gap. ALASCCA and 80702 randomized resected stage I-III. This patient is stage IV with active peritoneal disease. The biomarker match is real; the endpoint validation does not extend to the metastatic setting.
RoB2 D5, selective reporting / fragility: the Group A upper CI bound is 0.98. Direction is durable across three datasets, magnitude is not.
80702 celecoxib is a biomarker subgroup of a trial whose overall primary endpoint was negative. Pre-specified, but still a subgroup, with the effect-size precision caveats that implies.
Liao 2012 is ROBINS-I:Moderate observational. It earns its place as a third concordance signal, not as a standalone hazard estimate.

M1043I is exon 20 kinase-domain. ALASCCA Group A pools exon 9/20; the M1043I-specific subset within Group A is not reported, so the allele-class match is right but the exact-allele read is unmeasured.

picks.intervention_label: Botensilimab + balstilimab at 2L+ after FOLFIRI-bev progression, via Agenus NCT05608044 or CCTG NCT07152821 if eligible
picks.rationale: Best MSS-CRC immunotherapy signal on the table, and the reason it earns rank 2 is compartment-specific: this patient's peritoneal-only, post-liver-resection disease is exactly the no-liver-mets phenotype where the drug works. Bullock 2024 Nat Med (phase 1b expansion, r/r MSS mCRC, n=101) reported all-comer ORR 17%, 95% CI 10-26, with the NLM subset at ORR 22% and mOS 20.9 mo against ORR 5% when liver mets were active. The 2024 randomized phase 2 update (n=123 NLM, BOT+BAL vs BOT mono) held the combination at ORR 19% with mOS near 21 mo and specifically flagged responses at peritoneal sites, which is the patient's dominant disease compartment. That peritoneal-site call is the single most decision-relevant fact I can pull for this individual. Now the bias read: it is a single-arm phase 1b plus a randomized phase 2 against monotherapy, not against BSC or chemo. NLM was carved out as the responder phenotype post-hoc, not locked as a pre-specified primary stratum, so the 22% ORR and 20.9 mo mOS are subgroup numbers without CIs in the dossier row. The registrational test that matters, CCTG NCT07152821 vs BSC, has not read out. It sits below aspirin because it is a 2L+ proposition that only activates on progression past current 1L, not because the signal is weaker.
primary_concerns: No randomized readout against BSC or SoC yet. Single-arm phase 1b plus a phase 2 whose comparator is monotherapy; CCTG phase 3 NCT07152821 is the pending confirmatory test.
Selection on the NLM phenotype was post-hoc in the Bullock expansion, not a pre-specified primary stratum. The 22% subgroup ORR carries that caveat.
Dossier risk-of-bias is informal:med, not RoB2:Low, with open-label outcome ascertainment for ORR.
G3+ irAE 35% in phase 1 and 38% in the phase 2 update. That is the real toxicity envelope in a patient also heading into CRS.
Not a 1L pick. Sequencing-dependent, contingent on FOLFIRI-bev progression.

picks.intervention_label: Mutant-selective PI3K-alpha inhibition (inavolisib+bev on INTRINSIC NCT04929223, or RLY-2608 / tersolisib PIK3CA-mutant trials), contingent on M1043I confirmation and CRC arm-specific efficacy before commitment
picks.rationale: Ranked third at low confidence, and I want to be explicit about why the new evidence does not move it up. The PI3K-alpha mechanism now has fresh mutant-selective readouts, but they are all off-tumor abstracts. RLY-2608 + fulvestrant (Sammons 2025, ASCO abstract, breast, n=31) reported ORR 66.7% in the kinase-domain PIK3CA subgroup, 95% CI 38.4-88.2, mPFS 18.4 mo; tersolisib / STX-478 first-in-human (Montero 2024, ESMO abstract, n=61 breast/gyn) held activity across kinase- and helical-domain alleles at 21% all-comer ORR with a wild-type-sparing safety profile. That kinase-domain subgroup is the right allele class for M1043I, which is genuinely useful. But it is breast and gynecologic cancer, both are conference abstracts (informal:high risk-of-bias, not peer-reviewed), and predictive confidence for a rarer non-canonical allele like M1043I is lower than for canonical H1047R. The RCT-grade anchor is still INAVO120 (Jhaveri 2024 NEJM, HR_PFS 0.43, 95% CI 0.32-0.59, RoB2:Low), and it is HR+/HER2- breast cancer; the dossier case_match reads cross_tumor_only, which is correct. INTRINSIC pushes inavolisib+bev into PIK3CA-mut mCRC but has posted no arm-specific CRC PFS or OS. The CRC fallback is Juric 2018 alpelisib phase 1a: 2 PRs in the CRC subset of n=134, roughly 6% all-comer ORR, with G3+ hyperglycemia ~20% that stacks on bev. Enrolling here is a trial slot with hypothesis-grade CRC efficacy, not a treatment with established CRC OS benefit.
primary_concerns: Cross-tumor extrapolation across the board. INAVO120 is breast; RLY-2608 and tersolisib are breast/gyn abstracts. No RCT-grade CRC efficacy for any PI3K-alpha agent.
RLY-2608 66.7% and tersolisib 21% are single-arm conference-abstract ORRs (informal:high RoB, not peer-reviewed, no CRC subset), plus fulvestrant confounds the RLY-2608 combination readout.
INTRINSIC PIK3CA-mut mCRC arm-specific PFS/OS is unpublished. Trial-row evidence only.
M1043I is a recurrent but non-canonical kinase-domain hotspot; whether response at M1043I tracks the canonical H1047R / E545K / E542K alleles is uncharacterized at scale.

Combined metabolic-toxicity envelope: hyperglycemia ~6% G3+ on inavolisib and ~20% on alpelisib+bev, before any CRC efficacy is established. Tersolisib's wild-type-sparing profile is the mitigant, but only in an abstract.

notes:
Re-run over the expanded option set (16 new on-axis pan-RAS / PI3K-alpha trials, plus new clinical rows). My rank order is unchanged, and the new evidence is the reason it is unchanged rather than a reason to reshuffle.

The pan-RAS agents are the headline of this re-run, so I want to be precise about what the new data does and does not establish. Daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) now has a peer-reviewed pivotal readout: Wolpin 2026 NEJM, but that is RAS-mutant PDAC on codons 12/13/61 (2L RAS-G12 ORR 35%, 95% CI 17-56, n=26), not CRC and not A59T. The CRC-specific number is a corporate update (30 Sep 2024 cutoff, evidence_tier 4, no peer review, no disclosed N or CI): monotherapy ORR ~9%, which sits well below the PDAC figure and tempers any pan-RAS-in-CRC expectation before allele mismatch even enters. And the allele mismatch is the whole point. Knox 2025 J Med Chem shows daraxonrasib binds a CypA-SWI/SWII composite pocket and leaves the G12/G13/Q61 groove unoccupied, which is the structural rationale for reaching a switch-II allele; A59T was not tested. That is mechanistic plausibility, not empirical activity. Every clinical daraxonrasib dataset in this dossier enrolled canonical codons. So for KRAS A59T specifically the applicability is codon-agnostic binding inferred from structure, not allele-matched efficacy from a patient who carried the allele. The 16 new pan-RAS / MAPK trials (AN9025, YL-17231, PF-07934040, RO7673396, GH55, ERAS-0015, NST-628, darlifarnib/KO-2806, BPI-572270, the RAS(ON)+ivonescimab suite, and others) read 'codon-agnostic' or 'any RAS mutation' in their protocol text, which is why A59T plausibly clears the biomarker gate on paper. But that is a protocol-text eligibility question that turns on sponsor confirmation, and every one of these is a single-arm phase 1 or 1/2. Even if a sponsor accepts A59T, the design is dose-finding, not efficacy-controlled. NST-628 (pan-RAF/MEK glue) and darlifarnib (FTI) reach A59T only downstream of the RAS node, and their clinical readouts to date are melanoma corporate updates and G12C-restricted CRC (darlifarnib+adagrasib FIT-001, every enrolled CRC patient carried G12C), respectively. None of it is A59T evidence.

Anti-EGFR remains a no for A59T on population evidence, and nothing new changes that. Sorich 2015 meta-analysis (n=5,948, 9 RCTs, RoB2:Low) shows any-new-RAS OS HR 1.08 (95% CI 0.91-1.28) and PFS HR 1.03 (95% CI 0.78-1.36): no benefit. Schirripa 2015 (n=786, 0/9 NRAS-mut responders) and Arena 2021 (n=169, ROBINS-I:Moderate, 'occasional responders' at A59/A146 with weaker MAPK output than G12) extend and qualify the signal. The Lochhead 2018 A59T panitumumab case (n=1, -36% target lesion, 8 mo) is the single counter-anecdote, and it does not outweigh a 5,948-patient meta-analytic HR. Assess A59T individually, do not treat it as a flat contraindication, but do not offer routine anti-EGFR on a case report.

What stays dead-ended, unchanged from the prior read: TP53 R273 has no allele-matched pharmacology (eprenetapopt Park 2022 ORR 8%, R273 subset unanalyzed, program closed for solid tumors; rezatapopt is Y220C-specific by design). BCL2L1/TOP1 amp is hypothesis-grade across the class (navitoclax+irinotecan Vlahovic 2015 ORR 5% unselected, G3+ thrombocytopenia 24%; DT2216 first-in-human Khan 2025 n=20, SD only, no objective responses, no CRC cohort; AZD0466 abstract-only). Wnt/APC and SMAD4 remain mechanism-without-efficacy.

The surgical plan is still the most evidence-distorted choice on the table, and the new trials do not touch it. The HIPEC negative trifecta is unambiguous: PRODIGE 7 (Quenet 2021, n=265, RoB2:Low) OS 41.7 vs 41.2 mo, HR ~1.00, higher 60-day morbidity in the HIPEC arm; COLOPEC (Klaver 2019) 18-mo peritoneal DFS 80.9 vs 76.2%, NS; PROPHYLOCHIP-PRODIGE 15 (Goere 2020) 3-yr DFS 44 vs 53%, HR 0.97, p=0.82. CAIRO6 (Rovers 2024) added perioperative chemo around CRS-HIPEC and improved PFS/DFS but not OS. The OS signal lives in CRS, not HIPEC. That is a surgical decision the treating team owns, outside Libby feature-targeting scope, so I do not rank it, but the patient should be counseled that the HIPEC component is now a quality-of-evidence choice, not a default.

The backbone the patient should actually receive, explicitly out of Libby feature-targeting picks but the real treatment: FOLFIRI+bev (Hurwitz 2004, HR_OS 0.66, replicated Saltz 2008 and the FIRE-3 control arm); FOLFOXIRI+bev for a fit young ECOG-1 patient (TRIBE/TRIBE2 replicated, mOS 29.8 vs 25.8 mo, HR 0.80); CRS without HIPEC; sequential 2L/3L (VELOUR HR_OS 0.82; RAISE 0.84; SUNLIGHT 0.61; FRESCO-2 0.66; regorafenib CORRECT/CONCUR 0.77/0.55). The three feature-targeting picks above are additions to that backbone. Most defensible single feature-targeting recommendation: aspirin 160 mg QD post-CRS, RoB2:Low phase 3 with a biomarker match, qualified by the adjuvant-vs-metastatic indication gap. Least defensible: any pan-RAS asset offered as A59T-targeted therapy, because the A59T applicability rests entirely on codon-agnostic structural binding with zero allele-matched clinical readout, and the peer-reviewed pivotal data is PDAC on canonical codons.

picks.intervention_label: Comprehensive tumor NGS confirmation (extended RAS/BRAF, HER2, MMR/MSI, TMB, PIK3CA/APC/TP53/SMAD4)
picks.rationale: NCCN Colon v5.2025 treats extended RAS (KRAS/NRAS exons 2/3/4), BRAF, MMR/MSI, and HER2 testing as a category 1 expectation for every metastatic patient, and here nine features are still ngs_pending. Nothing downstream is decidable until the KRAS A59T VAF, a clean extended-RAS/BRAF read, and HER2 status come back on a single comprehensive panel. This is the one move where the guideline consensus is not in doubt.
primary_concerns: A59T sits in KRAS exon 3, so it already reads as RAS-mutant under NCCN v5.2025; the panel does not reopen anti-EGFR, it documents the exclusion cleanly.
HER2 amplification is the only pending result that could add a category 2A on-label option (DESTINY-CRC02 admits RAS-mutant patients), so it is worth chasing on the same block.

picks.intervention_label: Clinical-trial enrollment, biomarker-aligned (pan-RAS and mutant-selective PI3K-alpha programs)
picks.rationale: No approved therapy targets KRAS A59T or PIK3CA M1043I, so NCCN v5.2025 routes this patient to clinical-trial enrollment, which the guideline lists as an appropriate option at every line (category 2A). Sixteen newly-added pan-RAS and mutant-selective PI3K-alpha trials read A59T or M1043I as eligible on codon-agnostic text: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236), the RAS(ON) suite, tersolisib and RLY-2608. The highest-yield single action is a sponsor call confirming the switch-II A59 allele qualifies. I rank it second only because it depends on the workup finishing first.
primary_concerns: Every pan-RAS efficacy readout so far is codon 12/13/61 or a non-CRC tumor, so A59T activity is unproven; the guideline endorses the trial-enrollment pathway, not any validated A59T regimen.
The US-feasible slots (Revolution Medicines, Pfizer PF-07934040, Roche RO7673396) still turn on sponsor confirmation rather than published eligibility, so this is contingent, not settled.

picks.intervention_label: Cytoreductive surgery with honest HIPEC framing (perioperative systemic therapy per CAIRO6)
picks.rationale: Cytoreductive surgery for isolated peritoneal CRC carries the OS signal in PRODIGE 7 and is guideline-supported at experienced centers; the added oxaliplatin HIPEC did not (41.7 vs 41.2 mo, with higher 60-day morbidity). NCCN v5.2025 frames CRS-HIPEC as a selected-center option rather than a uniform recommendation, so the honest reading is to keep the cytoreduction and not oversell the HIPEC. CAIRO6 supports perioperative systemic therapy around the operation.
primary_concerns: PRODIGE 7 tested oxaliplatin HIPEC specifically; mitomycin C HIPEC was never randomized to a positive OS result either, so the agent choice is not a guideline-settled question.
This is a sequencing decision the surgical team owns, not a drug Libby ranks on its own.

picks.intervention_label: Tumor-informed serial ctDNA MRD (Signatera) bracketing CRS-HIPEC
picks.rationale: NCCN v5.2025 discusses tumor-informed ctDNA for surveillance, and peritoneal CRC is the setting where the recurrence lead-time signal reads strongest. Bracketing the surgery with Signatera (pre-CRS, day 30-60, then serial) gives an evidence-supported recurrence signal that complements CEA/CA-125 and imaging.
primary_concerns: ctDNA sits at category 2A for surveillance, not as a level-1 treatment-switch trigger, so it informs timing without changing the regimen by itself.

picks.intervention_label: Low-dose aspirin 160 mg/day for the PI3K-pathway-altered subset (ALASCCA)
picks.rationale: ALASCCA (2025, NEJM) is the first prospective biomarker-driven aspirin RCT in CRC to meet its endpoint: 160 mg/day roughly halved recurrence in the PIK3CA exon-9/20 subset (Group A), where M1043I sits (HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.24-0.98). The evidence is adjuvant and resected, so extending it to stage IV peritoneal disease is off-label, but the mechanism and the class safety are well characterized and it layers cheaply onto the post-HIPEC maintenance window.
primary_concerns: ALASCCA enrolled resected stage I-III disease, not stage IV, so the guideline signal does not yet cover the metastatic setting; this is a qualified add-on rather than a consensus recommendation.
GI-bleed risk across the perioperative window needs surgical sign-off before starting.

notes: Re-run over the refreshed option set (16 new on-axis pan-RAS / PI3K-alpha trials plus 10 new clinical-evidence rows). Guideline-anchored position: the only unambiguous consensus moves here are comprehensive NGS (NCCN cat 1) and clinical-trial enrollment (NCCN cat 2A), since no approved therapy covers KRAS A59T or PIK3CA M1043I and RAS-mutant status excludes anti-EGFR under both NCCN v5.2025 and the ESMO mCRC CPG. Standard chemo backbone (FOLFIRI-bev, already running) and anti-EGFR are out of Libby's targetable-feature scope and belong to the treating team. CRS with honest HIPEC framing and peri-operative ctDNA are guideline-supported sequencing anchors; ALASCCA aspirin is a biomarker-matched but off-label-in-metastatic add-on. Replaces the 2026-05-29 concensusite row.

picks.intervention_label: Daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) and other RAS(ON) inhibitors on codon-agnostic pan-RAS baskets — lead the inquiry with the trials whose written eligibility does not name a codon (Jacobio JAB-23E73 NCT06973564, Pfizer PF-07934040 NCT06447662 'any KRAS variant', Roche RO7673396 NCT06884618, RevMed RAS(ON)+ivonescimab NCT07397338, Adlai AN9025 NCT07252479)
picks.rationale: This is the pick the user has been waiting for. The prior codon-selective drugs could not touch a switch-II A59T, and the case sat in that gap. The new sweep brings in pan-RAS agents whose written eligibility asks only for a documented KRAS/NRAS/HRAS mutation — Pfizer's PF-07934040 spells out 'any KRAS variant' for its CRC cohort, which is the cleanest codon-agnostic gate on the board, and Jacobio, Roche, Adlai and the RevMed RAS(ON)+ivonescimab study read the same way. Mechanistically the RAS(ON) tri-complex binds GTP-loaded RAS regardless of the mutation site, and RMC-6236 regressed KRAS-mutant CRC/PDAC/NSCLC models across G12/G13/Q61 alleles (pmid:38778099, pmid:38778097); A59T applicability is a structural read-across, not direct A59T efficacy data, and I am saying that plainly. Prefers-trials, efficacy-leaning, surface-every-option — this pick clears all three, and the single sponsor call confirming A59T counts as a qualifying RAS allele is the highest-leverage action on the whole dossier.
primary_concerns: A59T eligibility rests on sponsor interpretation of codon-agnostic protocol text. The written gate reads open; whether a switch-II A59 allele counts as a qualifying RAS mutation is the one confirmation that makes or breaks enrollment, and it is a phone call, not a biopsy.

Several of the strongest-worded codon-agnostic baskets are China-sponsored (YL-17231, GH55, BPI-572270), which is an access barrier for a US patient — so I am leading with the US-feasible programs (Pfizer, Roche, Jacobio, RevMed, Adlai) and keeping the China rows as fallback.
Class-typical RAS(ON)/pan-RAS toxicity (rash, GI) is real but preferences.json carries no toxicity veto and the efficacy weight is 0.70, so this is counseling burden, not a blocker.

Sequencing: dose-finding enrollment competes with the planned CRS-HIPEC window. If the surgery is near-term, the honest framing is that a phase 1 slot may be a post-operative or post-progression option rather than something that displaces the operative plan now.

picks.intervention_label: CGT6297 (mutant-selective PI3K-alpha inhibitor) on the Cogent phase 1b with an explicit CRC+PIK3CA cohort (NCT07383506, Cohort 3)
picks.rationale: PIK3CA M1043I is a kinase-domain activating allele, and CGT6297 is the first trial on the board that names colorectal cancers with PIK3CA mutations as an eligible group by protocol text — not a breast-cohort read-across, an actual CRC-and-PIK3CA slot. That is a materially cleaner fit than routing M1043I through a breast-anchored inavolisib label, and it satisfies prefers-trials directly. Mutant-selective PI3K-alpha inhibition spares wild-type p110-alpha, which is the design generation that improves on alpelisib's metabolic burden, and the double-cis and kinase-domain PIK3CA biology supports M1043I as PI3K-alpha-inhibitor-sensitive (pmid:31699932). The axes to check before enrollment are diabetes status and any prior PI3K/AKT/mTOR exposure, neither of which is flagged in this patient. Tersolisib (STX-478, NCT05768139) and ETX-636 (NCT06993844) are the same mutant-selective class behind it if the Cogent cohort is full.
primary_concerns: M1043I needs to be locked as somatic and kinase-domain-activating on the comprehensive NGS for the oncogenic-PIK3CA gate to fire cleanly — target_validation carries the confirmatory panel as an essential row.

Cohort-specific eligibility: the CRC slot is Cohort 3 of a phase 1b, so confirm it is open and accruing before counting on it. If it is closed, tersolisib and ETX-636 Part A both take activating PIK3CA by tissue or ctDNA across solid tumors.
Hyperglycemia is the class signal even for mutant-selective agents; no toxicity veto bars it, but baseline glucose and the diabetes screen should be documented before start.

KRAS A59T co-activation historically blunts single-agent PI3K-alpha response in CRC, so the honest expectation is that this axis performs best in combination or in the mutant-selective generation — worth surfacing at consent rather than overselling monotherapy.

picks.intervention_label: Botensilimab + balstilimab on an MSS-CRC any-KRAS protocol (USC NCT06336902 accepts any KRAS mutation; Agenus NCT05608044 / expanded access NCT06751524), positioned at 2L+ after FOLFIRI-bev progression or as a post-HIPEC slot
picks.rationale: Bullock 2024 (pmid:38871975) put ORR 22% and mOS 20.9 mo on the board for the no-liver-mets MSS mCRC cohort, and the randomized phase 2 update called out peritoneal-site responses specifically. This patient is the exact phenotype that signal came from — liver mets resected, peritoneal-dominant disease — which is the strongest MSS-CRC immunotherapy read available and the one that actually maps to her disease compartment. The USC protocol takes any KRAS mutation on its face, so A59T is in without a codon argument. MSS keeps single-agent ICI off the table, and I am being clear that the Fc-enhanced CTLA-4 mechanism is what makes this an exception rather than the rule. Required prior fluoropyrimidine + oxaliplatin + irinotecan means she enrolls after progressing past 1L, so this is the 2L+ pivot, not a displacement of FOLFIRI-bev now.
primary_concerns: Sequencing and prior-therapy gate: the USC protocol requires prior oxaliplatin, which her FOLFIRI-bev history does not yet include — so realistically this is post-1L-progression or post-HIPEC, and the Agenus expanded-access route (NCT06751524) is the off-trial channel if standard options are exhausted first.
G3+ irAE around 35% (diarrhea/colitis, hepatitis); no veto bars it and the Fc-enhanced CTLA-4 management algorithms are codified, but it is a genuine counseling point at 0.70 efficacy weight.

The fasting-mimicking diet + IV vitamin C arm on the USC protocol adds patient burden that preferences.json does not flag against — surface it at consent rather than treating it as a blocker; the plain Agenus bot/bal protocol is the lower-burden alternative.

Peritoneal cavity is an immunologically distinct compartment (omental milky-spot biology), so response there is not guaranteed to track liver-met data — but the phase 2 update specifically reported peritoneal responses, which is the reassuring signal for this patient.

picks.intervention_label: Low-dose aspirin (160 mg PO daily) as a layered adjunct on the PIK3CA-mutant axis, sequenced around bevacizumab and the CRS-HIPEC bleeding window
picks.rationale: ALASCCA (pmid:40961426) is a 2025 phase 3 that met its primary endpoint: in resected CRC with a PI3K-pathway alteration, 160 mg aspirin cut time-to-recurrence with an HR of 0.49 in the PIK3CA exon-9/20 group — and M1043I is a kinase-domain (exon 20) allele that falls squarely in that Group A. The older Liao cohort (pmid:23094721) and the celecoxib subset of CALGB/SWOG 80702 (pmid:38889377) point the same direction. This is not a substitute for a targeted agent; it is a low-cost, oral, well-tolerated layer that the patient's own PIK3CA biology argues for, which is exactly the kind of option the surface-everything preference set asks me to carry. The metastatic setting differs from the resected adjuvant trials, so I am framing this as a post-HIPEC adjuvant-equivalent adjunct, not a metastatic-disease treatment claim.
primary_concerns: Bleeding risk is the real constraint: aspirin has to be sequenced around bevacizumab co-administration and paused across the CRS-HIPEC operative window per surgical protocol. This is a timing question the treating team owns, not a contraindication.
The evidence base is adjuvant/resected disease; extrapolating to a metastatic patient is a mechanism-and-safety argument, not a direct efficacy claim — I am labeling it as such.
Best deployed as an adjunct layered on top of the systemic backbone, not as a standalone move, so it should not compete for the primary-therapy slot.

picks.intervention_label: Proceed with cytoreductive surgery as planned; if HIPEC is added, advocate for a high-volume center and an honest discussion that the oxaliplatin HIPEC component is not OS-validated (consider mitomycin C or MRT-guided agent selection, NCT07291180)
picks.rationale: The user explicitly asked that the HIPEC plan be treated as a sequencing constraint and surfaced, not vetoed, and the efficacy-leaning preference set supports keeping it in play. The honest read: CRS holds the OS spine in colorectal peritoneal disease, but PRODIGE 7 (pmid:33476595) showed adding oxaliplatin HIPEC to CRS did not improve OS (41.7 vs 41.2 mo) and added 60-day morbidity, and COLOPEC and PROPHYLOCHIP round out a negative HIPEC trifecta. So my advocacy is not against the operation — it is for the patient walking in knowing the HIPEC drug component is a concentration-time bet rather than a proven OS gain. The Yale MRT-guided agent-selection study (NCT07291180) is worth flagging because her TOP1 co-amplification would intuitively favor an irinotecan-based intraperitoneal agent, and CAIRO6 supports the perioperative-systemic sequencing she is already on.
primary_concerns: This is a surgical/locoregional decision the treating team owns; my role is to make sure the OS-evidence caveat on the HIPEC drug component is spoken plainly, not to override the operative plan.

Agent selection interacts with her biology and prior exposure — TOP1 amplification favors an irinotecan-based intraperitoneal agent on rationale, but UGT1A1 genotype should be resolved first given irinotecan-HIPEC neutropenia/diarrhea risk.

Serial ctDNA (Signatera) across the peri-HIPEC window is the surveillance layer that tells us whether systemic therapy duration should extend — a low-cost add that the preference set's sequencing focus supports.

picks.intervention_label: Anti-EGFR (panitumumab or cetuximab) as an individualized, sponsor/PI-reviewed question rather than a flat exclusion — gated on locked extended-RAS/BRAF NGS and honest disclosure of the population-level signal
picks.rationale: The user asked for the full option space, and anti-EGFR is the one door that consensus tends to shut reflexively for atypical KRAS but that the A59T-specific literature says deserves an individual read. Lochhead 2018 (pmid:28404754) is a single-patient PR (~36%, 8-month duration) on panitumumab + FOLFIRI in an A59T tumor, and Arena 2021 (pmid:34031055) found variable, sometimes-preserved residual anti-EGFR sensitivity at A59/adjacent codons with weaker MAPK output than G12 mutants. I am carrying this honestly: the Sorich meta-analysis (pmid:25115304) shows non-canonical RAS mutations abrogate the population-level anti-EGFR benefit, so this is a low-probability, individually-reviewed play, not a recommendation to reflexively treat. Surfacing it lets the patient and PI make the call with the real evidence in front of them rather than having it pre-closed.
primary_concerns: The population signal points against benefit — Sorich HR 1.08 for OS in the new-RAS subset. I am not hiding that; the case for an individual trial rests on the A59T-specific functional heterogeneity, and the patient deserves both sides.
Requires the extended-RAS, NRAS/HRAS and BRAF V600 status fully locked on comprehensive NGS before anyone considers it — target_validation carries this as the gating essential row.
Best framed as a PI/tumor-board judgment call or a monitored anti-EGFR-containing platform (e.g., the pan-RAS + cetuximab arms on NCT07397338 / NCT06447662), not a solo off-label swing.
Skin toxicity and hypomagnesemia are class-typical; no veto bars them, but they factor into the risk/benefit of a low-probability play.

notes: Fresh round-1 re-run over the full current option set after the 16 new on-axis trials landed. The headline change from the prior run: I moved the pan-RAS RAS(ON) class to rank 1 because the new sweep finally gives A59T a set of trials whose written eligibility does not name a codon — that is the first real shot at her actual driver, and prefers-trials + efficacy-leaning + surface-everything all point the same way. Preference-fit read: efficacy_toxicity_weight 0.70 and prefers_trials are fully satisfied by ranks 1-3; toxicity_vetoes is empty and modality_constraints is empty, so nothing in the option set trips a hard preference filter. The one axis in genuine tension is not a preference violation but an evidence-honesty one: ranks 1 and 2 rest on codon-agnostic protocol text plus sponsor interpretation (A59T) and mechanistic read-across rather than direct A59T/M1043I efficacy data, and I have flagged that in every rationale rather than letting the trial-preference gloss over it. The free_text sequencing constraint (CRS-HIPEC window) is honored by positioning bot/bal and the pan-RAS phase 1 slots as post-1L / post-operative rather than displacing the planned operative course, and by keeping the HIPEC row itself in play with an honest OS-evidence caveat. MSS/TMB-low/PD-L1-neg correctly closes single-agent ICI; the A59T immuno-oncology-enrichment literature (pmid:33945173) describes the opposite phenotype and does not apply to this individual, so I did not lean on it.
